title: tune-nccl-collectives-and-stream-scheduling-for-tensor-parallel-overlap
author: Samir Patel
description: Motivation: tensor-parallel multi-GPU workloads were suffering from suboptimal overlap between NCCL collectives and local CUDA kernels, leading to reduced throughput at scale. This PR applies a set of coordinated changes to improve collectives scheduling, stream priority use, and lightweight synchronization so that communication/compute overlap is maximized without compromising correctness. Summary of changes: (1) introduce an explicit NCCLGroup wrapper around the tensor-parallel collective code paths to reduce per-operation launch overhead and better batch collectives for contiguous phases; (2) add a prioritized stream allocator for TP collectives vs compute kernels and prefer low-latency high-priority streams for small fan-in/fan-out ops while using medium-priority streams for large-volume all-reduce; (3) ensure kernel launches that can overlap with collectives are pinned to the compute stream and avoid unnecessary cudaStreamSynchronize calls; (4) add an ordered deferred-sync path that converts blocking syncs into cudaEvent synchronizations when safe; (5) small KV-cache touch-ups: avoid unnecessary cross-GPU synchronization when warming per-shard KV cache entries; (6) telemetry and perf counters to track overlapping ratios and NCCL op timings for future tuning. Results: measured on 8xA100 (v4-equivalent) with a 32k context and TP=8, end-to-end throughput improved by 7-12% on representative inference microbenchmarks and 10-18% reduction in tail latency P95 in the continuous batching harness. Benchmarks included both single-request large-context scenarios and steady-state continuous batching with mixed sequence lengths. Safety/testing/rollout: changes are guarded behind a runtime flag redwood.runtime.tp.nccl_overlap_v2=false by default; rollout plan is staged: enable for non-critical customers and nightly canary fleet, gather telemetry for 48 hours, and then flip by default if no regressions. This PR also includes unit tests for the new stream allocator and e2e stress tests in perf-canary. See linked Linear items for more context.

review_comments: Priya Nair: Can you explain why the prioritized allocator uses 3 priority levels rather than 2? Concerned about starvation of medium-priority compute kernels.

Samir Patel (author): Used 3 levels to separate small latency-sensitive collectives from large-volume collectives and compute. Implemented token-bucket guarding to prevent starvation; added more comments and unit tests to validate fairness.
Ethan Wong: Observed a flaky failure in tp_kv_warm_test on CI once. Could be ordering-related in the warm path.
Samir Patel (author): Found race where early exit path didn't record an event; fixed by always recording a sentinel event before skipping syncs. Added regression test.
Jean-Luc Moreau: Please add a short note in docs about the runtime flag and how to opt back out in case of regressions.
Samir Patel (author): Added docs/ops/rollouts.md with explicit rollback steps and telemetry queries to look for regressions.
merge_notes: Merged after approvals and CI green. Kept runtime flag off by default and created rollout checklist.
release_notes: Performance: Improved multi-GPU tensor-parallel NCCL overlap and stream scheduling leading to 7-12% throughput gains and up to 18% P95 tail latency reduction on large-context inference workloads. Behavior is behind a runtime flag and rollout is staged.
related_links: Linear: ENG-7821 - TP NCCL overlap tuning
notes_for_ops: Flag: redwood.runtime.tp.nccl_overlap_v2=false by default. To enable set to true on node pool config.
If regressions observed: flip flag off, drain affected nodes, revert patchset via rollback playbook in docs/ops/rollouts.md.
Telemetry queries: metrics.overlap_ratio by shard, metrics.nccl_op_ms p50/p95 across pools.
